To see what device documentation establishes about DNP3 security, we sampled 99 catalogue entries of 5 IED vendors and read their public documents (Appendix~\ref{app:crawler}). Of the 32 entries whose documents name DNP3, the documents establish DNP3 over TLS or IPsec for 6, DNP3 authentication without encryption for 1, encryption of another or an unnamed control protocol, or through a separate device, but not of DNP3 itself for 5, and an explicit statement that a DNP3 security feature is not provided for 1. For the remaining 19, the retrieved documents establish no DNP3 security; this is unknown, not evidence of plaintext operation, and for 11 of them some linked documents sit behind a vendor sign-in and were not read. Capability, default and deployment are separate questions. A documented capability says nothing about whether it is enabled: the Micro870 Controllers documentation, for example, states that DNP3 Secure Authentication is disabled by default. Deployment we did not measure: these are counts of sampled catalogue entries, not of vendors, installed devices or network traffic.
